original_question: Given a graph G known to be the visibility graph of a finite point set P in the plane, construct coordinates for a point set whose visibility graph is G.
target_in_paper: Section 2.1, Open Problem 3: the point-visibility-graph reconstruction problem, namely the task of drawing a point set in the plane whose visibility graph is the given graph G. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the right promised-input task: G is assumed to already be a visibility graph, and the goal is to produce a planar point-set realization of G. That matches reconstruction rather than recognition or characterization, and your phrase 'construct coordinates' is a precise version of the paper's 'draw the points in the plane.' ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
missing_details: The exact visibility relation should be stated: two vertices are adjacent exactly when the straight-line segment between their corresponding points contains or passes through no other point of the realizing point set. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

The output is any realizing point set, not necessarily the original hidden set P; the paper frames reconstruction as drawing 'one such set of points' whose visibility graph is G. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

To make the question stand-alone, it should specify a bijection between V(G) and the constructed points, since the paper defines the visibility graph by associating one vertex with each point. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
The ambient geometry should be made explicit as the Euclidean plane R^2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

No extra restrictions from outside the paper should be added: Open Problem 3 does not require general position, uniqueness of realization, rational or integer coordinates, or any complexity bound/encoding requirement. This is an inference from the official statement's scope and nearby context. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
refined_question: Given a finite simple undirected graph G=(V,E) that is promised to be the visibility graph of some finite point set in the Euclidean plane, construct coordinates for a point set Q={q_v : v in V} subset of R^2 such that for every distinct u,v in V, uv is an edge of G if and only if the straight-line segment q_u q_v contains no other point of Q; equivalently, output a planar point-set realization of G as a point visibility graph. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
justification: The draft is clearly targeting Section 2.1's reconstruction problem, not the neighboring recognition or characterization problems: the paper first distinguishes those three tasks, then explicitly says that 'actually drawing' such a point set is the visibility graph reconstruction problem, and immediately states Open Problem 3 in that form. The introduction supplies the operative notion of visibility for points and the definition of the point visibility graph. A faithful sharpening therefore keeps the scope narrow—promised input G, output some realizing point set in the plane—and only makes explicit the vertex-point correspondence and the adjacency/visibility condition needed for the question to stand alone. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
